1. What Is an SBP Exporters' Special FCVA Account?

Historically, Pakistani businesses receiving foreign currency export wire transfers faced strict foreign exchange rules: commercial banks automatically converted 100% of foreign currency (USD, EUR, GBP) into Pakistani Rupees (PKR) upon arrival.

To empower the IT export sector, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) enacted FE Circular No. 01 of 2023, creating the Exporters' Special Foreign Currency Account (FCVA) framework. Under this regime, certified IT exporters, software houses, and IT freelancers can retain up to 50% of foreign export proceeds in USD inside a dedicated foreign currency account.

2. Understanding the 50% Dollar Retention Framework

The mechanics of SBP FCVA retention operate on an automated split upon inward wire realization:

Automated 50% Split Example ($10,000 USD Export Remittance):

• $5,000 USD (50% Operational Allocation): Converted to PKR at prevailing interbank exchange rates and credited to your primary PKR business account for local salaries and office rent.

• $5,000 USD (50% FCVA Retention Allocation): Credited directly into your USD FCVA account in foreign currency, protecting your business against PKR exchange rate fluctuations.

3. Exhaustive List of Permissible FCVA Overseas Expenses

The SBP Foreign Exchange Manual explicitly permits FCVA USD funds to be spent abroad without requiring prior individual SBP clearance:

  • Cloud Infrastructure & Servers: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, DigitalOcean, Vercel, Linode.
  • Software & AI API Subscriptions: OpenAI API, GitHub Copilot, Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, Jira, Slack, Zoom, JetBrains.
  • Global Digital Advertising: Meta Ads (Facebook/Instagram), Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, X (Twitter) Ads.
  • Overseas Contractor & Consultant Payouts: Paying foreign freelancers on Upwork, Fiverr, or international consulting agencies.
